the doctrine of collateral estoppel prevents their relitigation in this case

1436: Issue preclusion: the district court in the Garmin case held Icon's assertion of the '351 patent barred by issue preclusion, and the Federal Circuit affirmed.

1504: Whether the Veterans Court's denial of recall of the mandate and the VACOLS-misstatement issue could be relitigated; court held the issue already decided in a prior appeal
This court has already considered this issue.

1767: Preclusion: the court held that the jury's invalidity rulings, left unreviewed as unnecessary to the judgment, have no issue-preclusive effect.
we rely on the well-established rule of federal preclusion law that will deny issue-preclusive effect to the invalidity rulings because we leave them unreviewed as unnecessary to the judgment.

Thus, Trobovic is collaterally estopped from raising these issues on appeal.

1859: Collateral estoppel (preclusion) from prior Reward Wall litigation and Rule 36 affirmance, invoked by Airlite
Accordingly, it is clear that a Rule 36 affirmance is a binding judgment for collateral estoppel purposes.
1873: Issue preclusion barring infringement claims based on the Lockheed Martin prior judgment (identity of issues) as to remaining accused particle counters

2066: Preclusion: the court held that its prior decision in Young, 494 F. App'x 65, binding on the question whether the agency may communicate with the examining psychiatrist, settled that issue against Young.
2191: Res judicata barred a crime victim's compensation claim because Colbert did not appeal the final CFC judgment in case No. 14-0062.

2217: Collateral estoppel: a district court judgment precluded Varnado from asserting that her May 2007 discrimination complaint related to her removal.
the district-court judgment collaterally estopped her from asserting that her May 2007 discrimination complaint related to her removal.
2230: Res judicata barred Padua's second MSPB appeal seeking a retirement annuity, because the issues were or could have been raised in his earlier appeal, which the Board decided on the merits. OPM and the Board invoked the doctrine.
the Board did not abuse its discretion or otherwise err in its determination that Mr. Padua's appeal was barred under the doctrine of res judicata.
2236: Collateral estoppel from the Teva invalidity judgment applied to dismiss the Epic, Mylan and Amneal actions.
Thus, we affirm the district court's dismissal of the remaining actions as barred by collateral estoppel.

2326: Interference estoppel by judgment: Fiers was precluded from pursuing hFIF protein claims not patentably distinct from counts lost in prior interferences.

2331: Mandate rule: whether the appellate mandate in S&N II barred the district court from considering Arthrex's challenge to the lost-profits award; the court held the mandate did not bar it.
Our mandate in S&N II did not resolve those issues, expressly or by implication.

we reject the district court's Rule 41 conclusion for a reason independent of any differences between NCR and Morpho-Trust.
2453: Res judicata (claim preclusion) bars plaintiff's suit seeking to relitigate issues decided in Upshaw I and affirmed in Upshaw II; invoked by the government.

2691: Collateral estoppel barred Mr. Allen from relitigating whether removal-related documents were properly retained outside his official personnel file, based on prior Board and Federal Circuit decisions.

2822: Claim preclusion from the 2006 Mentor-EVE litigation barring Mentor’s infringement allegations on the ’531 and ’176 patents for post-license acts; held not precluded.

2947: Whether prior district court non-indefiniteness holding precludes PTO reexamination ruling; held PTO not bound
In any event, the PTO is not bound here by the district court's decision.
3030: Collateral estoppel (issue preclusion) based on the S.D.N.Y. JPMC partial summary judgment finding that the '084 patent is ineligible under section 101; the court held the finality requirement was met and preclusion applied.
we conclude that collateral estoppel attaches as a result of the JPMC court's partial summary judgment order invalidating the '084 patent.
3063: Collateral estoppel invoked by Par to bar Novartis from relitigating whether acetaldehyde is an antioxidant in the 13.3 mg declaratory judgment action; the court held the collateral estoppel ruling correct.
Thus, the ruling on collateral estoppel was correct.
3084: Res judicata (claim preclusion) barred the employee's second petition for enforcement of the 2008 back-pay order because it could have been raised in his first petition, which resolved on the merits.
Because the Board properly denied Mr. Slocum's petition under the doctrine of res judicata, we affirm.
3092: Issue preclusion: the district court dismissed Icon's claims against Garmin as barred by issue preclusion based on the Polar indefiniteness ruling; affirmed.
The ruling of the district court that Icon's assertion of the '351 patent is barred by the doctrine of issue preclusion in Icon Health & Fitness, Inc. v. Garmin Int'l ... is also affirmed.
3113: Collateral estoppel: the district court's judgment in the Apotex and Teva actions rested on collateral estoppel from the invalidity ruling in the Sandoz litigation; the court vacated that judgment and remanded, so preclusion was not applied on the existing judgment.

Because Momenta is not seeking to relitigate an issue that was already conclusively decided in Momenta I, law of the case does not apply.

Res judicata does not automatically arise against unknown future situations.

Mr. Renville’s claim under USERRA is also barred under the doctrine of res judicata.
3290: Res judicata barred Bishop's third IRA appeal based on the prior final MSPB decisions; the agency/MSPB invoked preclusion, and the court rejected Bishop's argument that the earlier decision lacked jurisdiction.
We agree with the MSPB's ruling that Mr. Bishop's most recent IRA appeal is again barred by the doctrine of res judicata.

3320: Collateral estoppel applied by the Board to bar relitigation of whether Payton established Board jurisdiction over her failure-to-restore claim, based on prior appeals.

3519: Issue preclusion / law of the case: whether prior decision finding claims not indefinite binds the supplemental damages proceeding; court held change in law under Nautilus exception applies so prior ruling not binding

4564: Collateral estoppel from the Rule 36 judgment in VirnetX I precluding VirnetX from relitigating whether RFC 2401 was a printed publication, as invoked by Apple.

5351: Claim preclusion from the 2012 lawsuit barring infringement allegations on the '422, '116 and '769 patents; court found the district court applied the wrong standard, vacated the dismissal and remanded without deciding preclusion itself.

5358: Claim preclusion: Board held that the prior district-court default judgment finding the SPORT COURT mark distinctive and not generic precludes the genericness cancellation petition; court affirmed.

5429: Collateral estoppel from affirmed PTAB invalidity decision precludes patentee from asserting '183 patent claims in district court

5644: Kessler doctrine: whether Kessler bars assertion of the patents against pre-judgment GCM activity. Court declined to extend Kessler to activity predating the earlier judgment, which was Google's argument; Kessler may apply only to post-judgment activity if claim preclusion is later shown.

5692: Judicial estoppel (preclusion-type doctrine invoked by Cisco) barring Egenera from correcting inventorship; court held the New Hampshire factors were not met and estoppel does not apply

5768: Collateral estoppel from prior Federal Circuit decisions (Swartz I and II) barring relitigation of utility and enablement for the '058 and '765 applications and related applications.

5911: Issue preclusion barred the illegal exaction claim because the district court had already decided that Nelson continued to owe the debt.

5996: Collateral estoppel barred the employees' second USERRA constructive-discharge appeals based on the hostile-work-environment issue decided in Bryant I; the change-of-law exception and detrimental-reliance arguments were rejected.

6011: Claim preclusion (res judicata) barred the employee's back-pay and related claims from the 2006-2007 indefinite suspension because they could have been raised in his first Board appeal; the district-court jurisdictional exception did not apply.

6051: Preclusion: issue preclusion from prior litigation barring Apple's invalidity challenges (obviousness and non-joinder)

6107: Sovereign immunity of a state patent owner in IPR proceedings, held not to apply based on binding precedent (University of Minnesota); procedural threshold challenge to IPR institution/proceeding, coded as preclusion-type binding precedent question is not a fit, so coded as other procedural threshold issue
6124: Preclusion: Batcher argued the 2006 New York state-court stipulation had preclusive (res judicata/waiver) effect barring Ms. Batcher's apportionment claim; the court rejected the argument and held the stipulation did not preclude apportionment.

6150: Claim preclusion bars UDPA, Patent Act (false marking) and Lanham Act claims based on the final judgment in Gravelle II; Belflower and Murray held to be privies of Kaba.

6151: Canadian Competition Act claim held precluded under the rule against claim splitting, though not asserted in Gravelle II.

6249: Res judicata bars Searcy's claims against the agency, invoked by the agency, so the claims are precluded.

6317: Collateral estoppel (issue preclusion) from the prior appeal involving the '013 patent bars relitigating the construction of 'aseptic'; invoked by petitioner Nestle.

6452: Whether the prior appellate mandate precluded the Claims Court from adjudicating the breach of contract, breach of fiduciary duty, and breach of trust claims; the court held the mandate did not reach them and they were not previously adjudicated.

6517: Issue preclusion from the prior litigation's §101 ruling: the court held the prior judgment does not preclude relitigating patent eligibility because the §101 issue was not actually litigated and was not necessary to the prior judgment (the court rejected the district court's intervening-change-in-law rationale).

We therefore conclude that issue preclusion does not apply in this case, not because there was a change in law as the district court held, but because the issue of patent eligibility under § 101 was not actually litigated and it was not necessary to the judgment rendered.
6524: Issue preclusion: the agency invoked collateral estoppel based on the 2014 Board decision that Greer waived appeal rights; the court held the MSPB properly applied issue preclusion.
Further litigation of the issue was therefore barred by the doctrine of issue preclusion.
6527: Preclusion: collateral estoppel, invoked by Polygroup, barred Willis from relitigating the tree-portion construction and the requirement to consider obviousness over Miller alone, based on the earlier appeal in No. 2018-1745.
that argument has been resolved against Willis as a matter of collateral estoppel.
6545: Preclusion: liability on the '029 patent claims and the '290 patent claim 10 is precluded because the Board's unpatentability determinations were affirmed; Imperium's cross-appeal argument for liability on the '290 patent was rejected.
Liability based on those claims, therefore, is now precluded. See Fresenius USA, Inc. v. Baxter Int'l, Inc., 721 F.3d 1330, 1339 (Fed. Cir. 2013).
6602: Collateral estoppel (preclusion) from the Massachusetts §101 decision as applied to claims 31 and 32 of the '850 patent and claims 12, 23 and 1 of the '996 patent; invoked by ScottCare and held precluded.

Because the judgment underlying the district court's application of collateral estoppel has been affirmed and CardioNet does not otherwise argue that the district court erred in its application of the doctrine, we affirm the district court's judgment of invalidity of claims 31 and 32 of the '850 patent and claims 12 and 23 of the '996 patent.
6603: Collateral estoppel from the Massachusetts §101 decision as applied to all asserted claims of the '207 patent; the underlying judgment was reversed, so the preclusion-based ineligibility judgment was vacated and remanded.

Because the judgment underlying the district court's application of collateral estoppel has been reversed, we vacate the district court's judgment of ineligibility of all of the asserted claims of the '207 patent and remand for further proceedings.
6605: Preclusion: Ahuruonye argued a prior Board jurisdictional finding collaterally estopped the Board from treating the Charge Two emails as unprotected; court rejected the argument
Ahuruonye mischaracterizes the impact of the Board's prior findings, however.
6647: Collateral estoppel from the prior MSPB decision barred relitigating whether Keys' resignation was voluntary (constructive removal claim); invoked by the agency
Accordingly, we agree that collateral estoppel precludes Keys from again disputing whether his resignation was voluntary.
6701: Collateral attack on a prior final Veterans Court decision denying fee waiver and imposing a filing-motion requirement; the earlier final decision bars relitigation.
El Malik did not appeal that decision, and it thereafter became final.
6805: Collateral estoppel from Lentz I barred relitigation of constructive discharge in Lentz II; court held the issue was not identical and not preclusive.
Therefore, collateral estoppel cannot apply to the constructive discharge claim.
6827: Preclusion: whether the California Unemployment Insurance Appeals Board finding should have collateral estoppel effect in the MSPB proceeding; the court held it was not preclusive.
the CUIAB decision does not have preclusive effect on the Board.
6830: Preclusion: the court held Gurvey precluded from arguing that the MetroCard technology is owned or controlled by NYC, based on a prior state court factual finding.
she is precluded from arguing that the MetroCard technology is owned or controlled by NYC based on the prior state court decision, which made a contrary factual finding.
6869: Commission denied DeLorme's petition to rescind or modify a civil penalty order on the ground that the matter was res judicata. The court held that neither claim nor issue preclusion applies because this is a continuation of the same investigation, and that law of the case does not apply because the issue was never decided.

We conclude that the Commission erred by relying on res judicata because neither the Commission nor this court has considered whether to rescind or modify the civil penalty in light of the invalidity of the relevant patent claims.
6892: Res judicata precluding Searcy's USERRA claims from relitigation; court rejected argument that res judicata cannot apply to USERRA claims.
To the extent Searcy suggests that res judicata cannot apply to USERRA claims, that argument is without merit.
7092: Claim preclusion from the Delaware judgment on the parent '514 patent; the court held the '305 claims are patentably indistinct so claim preclusion likely bars the suit.
We further hold that claim preclusion likely bars Indivior’s suit as the ’514 claims and the ’305 claims are patentably indistinct.
7180: Res judicata: a prior dismissal for failure to prosecute (failure to oppose motions to dismiss) operates as an adjudication on the merits and precludes the later infringement suit against CARB.
We conclude that the district court properly applied preclusion on this ground.
7181: Res judicata applied to infringement damages claims for conduct after the prior judgment, because the accused CARB Cap-and-Trade activity is essentially the same and was previously adjudged not infringing.
The district court properly held that the dismissal in Sowinski I is res judicata, for CARB is charged with the same acts of infringement of the same patent.
7212: Claim preclusion (res judicata) barred FMC's breach of guaranty agreement claims against Ginnie Mae because Ginnie Mae and the SEC were in privity and the SEC civil enforcement consent judgment was a final judgment arising from the same transactional facts.
Accordingly, the Court of Federal Claims properly concluded that the SEC and Ginnie Mae are in privity for the purposes of claim preclusion.
7237: Freezing Patent: affirmance of PTAB unpatentability decision given issue-preclusive effect against XY in this co-pending case, applied sua sponte
That affirmance renders final a judgment on the invalidity of the Freezing Patent, and has an immediate issue-preclusive effect on any pending or co-pending actions involving the patent.
7332: Claim preclusion (and Kessler doctrine) barring Huang's infringement claims in Case 2 based on the prior Case 1 judgment of noninfringement, invoked by Huawei.

we hold that the district court did not abuse its discretion when it denied Mr. Huang's motion to transfer venue and did not err in deciding that Mr. Huang is precluded from pursuing his claims of infringement in Case 2.
7338: Whether Purdue was collaterally estopped from challenging Joshi's status as prior art based on the prior district court litigation over the '888 patent
We agree with Purdue that the issue of Joshi's priority was not actually litigated in the district court case involving the '888 patent
7358: Collateral estoppel from the Virginia judgment barred Capital One's Sherman Act antitrust claims on the relevant market issue; the court applied preclusion to alternative grounds and sustained the judgment.
Applying the principles of collateral estoppel as we believe the Fourth Circuit would apply them, we sustain the judgment as to Capital One's Sherman Act claims based on collateral estoppel.
7359: Collateral estoppel from the Virginia judgment also barred Capital One's Clayton Act section 7 claim, on the same relevant market failure.
For similar reasons, collateral estoppel applies to Capital One's claim under section 7 of the Clayton Act.
7396: Whether the prior unreasonable-delay judgment bars the present APA challenge to the denial of the rulemaking petition under claim preclusion, with the PTO as the party invoking preclusion.
Accordingly, claim preclusion does not bar his present claims.
7465: Preclusion: res judicata and collateral estoppel argument that the agency punished her twice for the same act was rejected because neither the study hall denial nor the counseling memorandum involved litigation.
Res judicata and collateral estoppel require litigation of some sort.
7540: Judicial estoppel applied by district court against Biogen distinguishing clinical from therapeutic efficacy; majority found the error harmless and ancillary, dissent would reverse on it

Biogen raises several ancillary issues in an effort to reverse the district court decision... our conclusion that the district court did not clearly err in finding the '514 Patent invalid for lack of written description under § 112 renders all these arguments superfluous.
7645: Preclusion: Watkins argued that the D.C. Superior Court and D.C. Court of Appeals whistleblower decisions and a prior Federal Circuit decision precluded a finding that his employment ended November 6, 2005; court rejected the preclusion argument.
Contrary to Mr. Watkins's assertions, the decisions addressing his whistleblower case did not deem his employment as continuing beyond November 6, 2005.
7731: Res judicata (claim preclusion) bars relitigation of the default termination claims from the first suit.
the doctrine of res judicata, based on policies of judicial economy and finality, properly precludes what amounts to an attempt to relitigate the claim he presented earlier.
7771: Collateral estoppel from the prior '1892 IPR final written decision barring M2M from arguing Kloba fails to disclose 'consumer usage information' in the '477 patent; precluded, invoked by Amazon.

We therefore find that this same issue was actually litigated in the '1892 IPR and agree with the Board that M2M is collaterally estopped from arguing that Kloba failed to disclose 'consumer usage information'
7842: Claim preclusion barred the second suit alleging infringement of the same patent by the same taxi display mounts after a prior summary judgment of non-infringement.
we agree with the district court that claim preclusion bars adjudication of Mr. Ottah's 2021 lawsuit.
8041: Whether issue preclusion based on the earlier Wilhelm v. Caldera litigation applied to bar or affect whether Dr. Wilhelm was competent to give a medical opinion; the court held the issues were not identical.
The issues are not the same, and for at least that reason, issue preclusion could not apply.
8062: Collateral estoppel: Barrett precluded from relitigating whether HERA's Succession Clause bars his non-constitutional derivative claims, based on Perry II
We agree with the government that Barrett is collaterally estopped from re-litigating whether HERA's Succession Clause bars his non-constitutional derivative claims.
8098: Collateral estoppel barring Surti from relitigating trade secret and contract claims previously decided and affirmed in Fleet I.
Surti is collaterally estopped from relitigating those issues.
8120: Collateral estoppel: the Board precluded Neese from relitigating timeliness of her MSPB appeal, which was decided in Neese I.
Thus, the Board did not err in its application of collateral estoppel and Ms. Neese cannot now relitigate this issue.
8342: Res judicata precludes relitigating the sufficiency of the original Apple complaint, which was identical to the complaint held frivolous in the 2019 case (Apple case, No. 22-1229).
His effort to relitigate the sufficiency of the original complaint is precluded under the doctrine of res judicata.
8349: Apple's issue preclusion and cross-appeal rule arguments based on the Board's prior unpatentability finding for claim 1 of each patent; court rejected preclusion because the claims differ.
Because “identity of issues” is lacking given this important difference between the claims, issue preclusion and the cross-appeal rule are inapplicable.
8357: Preclusion effect of the prior withdrawal with prejudice on relitigating the same VEOA issues in the 2019 appeal
The administrative judge pointed out that Mr. Turner had withdrawn his 2016 appeal, which was then dismissed with prejudice.
8384: Collateral estoppel: the C.D. Cal. court held claims 1-9 and 12 of U.S. Patent No. 6,611,231 invalid as indefinite based on the collateral-estoppel effect of a N.D. Cal. judgment, and the Federal Circuit affirmed on that basis because its companion appeal affirmed the N.D. Cal. judgment.
There is no dispute that our affirmance in the companion appeal compels affirming in this appeal.
8451: Judicial estoppel (preclusion-type doctrine invoked by MasterCard based on AlexSam's statements to the PTAB); court held AlexSam was not estopped because its positions were consistent.
In doing so here, we view AlexSam as maintaining consistent positions in its arguments before the Board and its arguments before the district court.
8539: Preclusion: whether Minnesota is collaterally estopped from raising sovereign immunity from IPR, given prior litigation
Because this issue has been litigated to finality and determined on the merits, Minnesota is collaterally estopped from making an immunity argument here.
8560: Collateral estoppel: Board dismissed the second annuity appeal as collaterally estopped by a pending first Board appeal; the court held the earlier AJ decision was not a final judgment and so could not ground preclusion.
Here, as the government agrees, the Board erred in dismissing the suit based on collateral estoppel because Castillejos III, which is still pending review by the full Board, is not a final judgment.
8561: Administrative (adjudicatory-efficiency) preclusion: government urged affirmance on the ground that repetitive second appeals may be dismissed for adjudicatory efficiency; the court declined because the claims were facially different (1987-1992 service versus 1974-1986 service).
Under these circumstances, we decline to affirm the Board's dismissal on grounds of adjudicatory efficiency.
8594: Preclusion of a collateral attack on the cancellation of the earlier '181 solicitation, based on the prior Court of Federal Claims judgment that Veteran Shredding lost for lack of standing and did not appeal.
To the extent that Veteran Shredding appears to challenge the cancellation of the prior '181 solicitation, it is precluded from doing so.
8609: Res judicata: government argued Shell I judgment barred claims for post-November 2015 remediation costs; court held partial breach doctrine applies and claims were not precluded.
We therefore agree with the Claims Court that the Oil Companies' successive partial breach claim was not barred by res judicata.
8794: Law-of-the-case doctrine: whether the Board's 1997 statement that the 1975 rating decision was the last final denial bound later tribunals; the court held the doctrine did not establish that finding.
Therefore, we affirm the Veterans Court's law-of-the-case conclusion.
8817: Collateral estoppel barred Gossage from relitigating whether his DOL administrative complaint was untimely, based on prior Board decisions; the Board's preclusion ruling was affirmed.
we find that the Board correctly applied collateral estoppel to bar Gossage from relitigating the untimeliness of his administrative complaint.
8866: Claim preclusion barred Crumley's second wrongful-discharge suit (seeking reinstatement, record correction and back pay) based on the final judgment in Crumley II, because the new allegations were not materially relevant to the same claim.

Accordingly, we affirm. In this case, without any developed argument from Mr. Crumley on the materiality issue—and there is none—he has given us no basis to disturb the Court of Federal Claims' claim-preclusion determination and resultant dismissal.
8935: Collateral estoppel barred relitigation of the retaliatory-removal claim in the IRA appeal, based on the final decision in the separate Removal Appeal; invoked by the government.

8992: Discretionary declining of declaratory judgment jurisdiction; district court's discretion-based dismissal vacated for inadequate explanation
9035: Prior federal judgment in the interpleader action (Bestway) that Sgromo did not own the patents is final and not subject to relitigation in this court.
That final judgement is not subject to relitigation in this court.
9036: Issue preclusion: the Board was collaterally estopped by prior inter partes reexamination decisions (the '702 and '290 patents) from finding that an artisan would combine Steigerwald and Cobos, so the Board's obviousness decision on claims 1-19, 28, and 31 was vacated. 9094: Preclusion: the Board properly applied issue preclusion to findings of the Tax Court on understatement and reasonable cause, and pro se status did not bar preclusion.
We discern no reversible Board error regarding the application of this doctrine in the present case.
9123: Collateral estoppel from a prior Board jurisdictional dismissal. The Board held Haynes collaterally estopped from relitigating jurisdiction; the Federal Circuit held the Board erred because the two appeals were not shown to involve the same underlying cause of action.

Given the record before us, because we cannot say that Mr. Haynes's 2014 and 2021 appeals involve the same underlying cause of action, we conclude that the Board erred in resting its decision on collateral estoppel.
9140: Kessler doctrine preclusion: prior with-prejudice dismissal precludes the infringement claims for the same patent claims against essentially the same products
We agree with the district court that the Kessler doctrine precludes him from doing so.
9144: Collateral estoppel bars Askan from relitigating in the Claims Court whether 28 U.S.C. § 1500 deprives the court of jurisdiction, because the issue was decided in Askan I; the government invoked preclusion.

We hold that the Claims Court correctly found that relitigation of the issue in this case—whether Section 1500 deprives the Claims Court of jurisdiction over the second Claims Court complaint—was barred by collateral estoppel.
9216: Issue preclusion: court held the Claims Court's preclusion-based dismissal of the expanded accounting claim was vacated; scope of a damages accounting not automatically limited by the Fletcher litigation accounting.

9321: Claim preclusion (res judicata) barred the second suit alleging infringement of the '840 patent by the same laptop mounting device, based on the prior dismissal for failure to state a claim; National Grid invoked preclusion.
we agree with the district court that claim preclusion bars Mr. Ottah's suit underlying this appeal.
9710: Res judicata (claim preclusion) bars third individual right of action based on prior Board decision in Brown-2 affirmed by this court
Because the Board correctly applied the doctrine of res judicata, we affirm on that ground.
9727: Res judicata barred the patent infringement claims under 28 U.S.C. 1498 because the same patent and same accused device were litigated to final judgment in Bondyopadhyay I.
The Claims Court correctly determined that Dr. Bondyopadhyay's claims accusing the United States of infringing the '134 patent were barred by the doctrine of res judicata.
9729: The patent-infringement-based takings claim was barred by res judicata because it is a patent infringement claim previously adjudicated.
As patent infringement, those claims have previously been adjudicated and, as indicated above, are now barred under res judicata.
9762: Issue preclusion bars relitigating whether the Breathe Right dilator infringes Glover's patents, based on the prior Ohio judgment of no infringement; invoked by defendants.
Glover litigated the same issue – patent infringement by the Breathe Right® dilator – in the Northern District of Ohio action and cannot relitigate that issue now.
9808: Preclusion/finality: whether the 2010 final TDIU adjudication implicitly denied and terminated the earlier pending 1976 informal TDIU claim under the Williams implicit-denial rule; the court holds the earlier claim was terminated, so the VA's finality position prevails.
We agree with the Veterans Court, however, that the VA's 2010 final adjudication of Mr. Bryce's November 2006 TDIU claim terminated his pending November 1976 informal TDIU claim.
9810: Res judicata barred the infringement and Takings-type claims regarding the '134 patent based on prior adjudications and a 2014 non-infringement judgment; invoked by the government.
We affirm the district court's dismissal based on res judicata.
9878: Collateral estoppel based on invalidity (indefiniteness) judgment in ESET case; the underlying judgment was vacated, so collateral estoppel cannot apply. Vacated invalidity judgment and remanded.
We cannot uphold applying collateral estoppel based on a vacated judgment.
9892: Whether the Ninth Circuit's dismissal of Siegler's appeal precluded review of her non-patent claims under law of the case or collateral estoppel, invoked by appellees.

Here, the Ninth Circuit's dismissal of Siegler's appeal does not operate as a decision on the merits of Siegler's nonpatent claims, particularly where our sister circuit lacked jurisdiction over any of Siegler's claims.
9911: Res judicata bars relitigation of Searcy's claims arising from his 1977 separation, including USERRA/VEOA arguments
The Board also did not err in concluding that Mr. Searcy's claim was barred by the doctrine of res judicata.
10140: Collateral estoppel (preclusion) from the prior Google claim construction order, invoked by Meta. The court held that estoppel does not apply because the issues are not identical.

Meta asks us to apply an estoppel effect to a prior court’s construction of a different term in a different patent with different surrounding claim language. We decline to do so, as we do not find the issues to be identical.
10409: Whether StrongVolt was precluded from challenging the registration's remaining goods because it consented to deleting other goods from the registration

Mr. Ghomeshi cites no authority for his proposition, which is particularly dubious in light of StrongVolt's express statement that its consent shall not be interpreted as conceding on the issue of validity of the remaining goods.
10500: Whether the NDA forum selection clause bars Samsung's IPR petitions at the PTAB; district court denied preliminary injunction compelling Samsung to seek dismissal of the IPRs. Court held the forum selection clause does not govern the IPR proceedings.

10514: Preclusion: Golden argued a prior Federal Circuit holding that a separate complaint against Google was not facially frivolous precluded dismissal here; court held it did not.

10600: Collateral estoppel: Medline precluded from raising its argument that Solazzo is incompatible with the other references, including on remand.
Accordingly, Medline is also precluded from making that argument on remand.
10627: Collateral estoppel from the Board's final written decision in the related '483 IPR applied to hold claim 18 (and by agreement claim 14) of the '816 patent unpatentable; invoked by Google (Side B).

Since the issues of patentability of claim 18 of the ’483 patent and claim 18 of the ’816 patent are identical and the other elements of collateral are undisputed, collateral estoppel applies and we accordingly hold claim 18 of the ’816 patent unpatentable.
10804: Preclusion: the court held that collateral estoppel from the Apple decision applied in the Motorola and Blackboard cases, invoked by the defendants, so Uniloc was precluded from arguing it granted no license and retained standing.

There is no question here that the Apple case addressed and decided the very same issues as are presented here; those issues were actually litigated; the issues were determined by a valid and final judgment; and the determination of all three issues was essential to the prior judgment.
11008: Claim preclusion (res judicata): whether the ABS I judgment precluded Inguran's induced infringement claim in ABS III. Court held the claim was not barred because it rests on different transactional facts and could not have been asserted in ABS I.

11078: Preclusion: the court held it could not entertain Evans's direct-payment argument because the earlier Haggart III judgment directing payment through class counsel was already affirmed in Haggart IV.

11145: Issue preclusion from the unappealed '929 PTAB reconsideration decision; court held preclusion did not apply under Restatement §28 equitable exceptions

11180: Preclusion of Shu's back pay start-date argument by the final 2014 Board order that he did not appeal.
this very issue was raised and finally decided by the Board’s 2014 Order, which Mr. Shu did not contest.
11253: Issue preclusion from the district court litigation: the Claims Court wrongly found the spoliation of the handgun did not change the evidentiary landscape, so issue preclusion does not bar relitigation of the central issues.

11268: Preclusion: res judicata barred the second IRA claim based on the first IRA claim's final decision on the merits.

11281: Collateral estoppel barred Akerman's new IRA appeal and his request to reopen the prior IRA docket; the Board invoked preclusion and the court affirmed.

11439: Issue preclusion from IBLA findings: court held the Court of Federal Claims erred by not conducting a proper issue preclusion analysis and vacated for it to consider the preclusive effect of the IBLA findings.

11570: Issue preclusion barred appellants from arguing that the Board's rehearing request was ultra vires, based on Odyssey Logistics; invoked by the PTO.

11844: Preclusion: Monbo's law of the case, res judicata, collateral estoppel and judicial estoppel arguments based on a D.C. District Court dismissal were rejected
11851: Res judicata (claim preclusion) applied to bar the complaint, which echoed claims from two prior Claims Court suits; invoked by the government.

11911: Preclusion: whether the prior IPR determination on claim 10 precluded Willis from relying on one-step functionality in apportioning damages; held not precluded.

11999: Preclusion: the veteran argued that res judicata barred the Veterans Court from changing its prior interlocutory ruling in the same proceeding; the court rejected that argument, holding that res judicata does not bar reconsideration within the same proceeding.
they do not bar reconsideration of rulings (let alone interlocutory ones) within the same proceeding.
12083: Issue preclusion: whether the Nehmer court's decisions precluded VA from denying Constantine the Nehmer class effective date; the court held he was not entitled to issue preclusion because the Korean DMZ coverage issue was never actually litigated and determined against the government.

12161: Preclusion: argument that the December 16 Order precluded dismissal under law of the case or collateral estoppel was rejected.

12234: Issue preclusion: affirmance of the invalidity ruling on claim 17 in the companion Florida case collaterally estops mCom from asserting claim 17 against HSBC, invoked by HSBC.

12298: Collateral estoppel from the Board's IPR claim construction decision is inapplicable because the district court applies Phillips rather than broadest reasonable interpretation

12318: Whether Board claim constructions under the broadest reasonable interpretation standard have issue-preclusive effect in district court; the court held they do not, because district courts apply Phillips.

12357: Claim preclusion barred a second suit seeking credit for Question 27 on the Customs Broker License Examination, which was the same claim litigated in Chae I. The government invoked preclusion.

12374: Res judicata barred Mora Jr.'s claim for a deferred retirement annuity based on his father's prior final Board decision denying the father's CSRA annuity application.

12476: Preclusion: Monbo argued a prior District of Columbia ruling found her an interested party and should bind the agencies and Claims Court; court rejected this because the district court expressly declined to decide that issue.

12597: Claim preclusion (res judicata) bars Engen's tax refund claims based on prior W.D. Wash. judgment; invoked by the government

12632: Res judicata (claim preclusion) barred relitigation of Casimier's entitlement to CSRS annuity benefits, invoked by OPM and upheld by the MSPB and the court.

12772: Defendants' argument that Sunoco was collaterally estopped from tying damages to unapportioned BSAs based on U.S. Venture II; rejected
At a minimum, we are unpersuaded that Defendants-Cross-Appellants can show factor one is satisfied here.
12867: Res judicata (claim preclusion) barred Avery's second suit seeking the Airman's Medal and related retirement pay, based on the prior dismissal in Avery I; invoked by the government.

13150: Res judicata barred Berry's Veterans Court appeal seeking to revisit the merits of the September 2018 Board decision, which this court had already finally decided; a prior jurisdictional dismissal carries preclusive effect as to the jurisdictional issue.

13344: Res judicata and collateral estoppel applied by the Board to bar relitigation of USERRA challenges to thirteen FAA nonselections; the court affirmed that preclusion applied and rejected the claimed 'false narrative' and new-evidence exceptions.

13359: Res judicata bars relitigation of the VA finality rule challenge previously resolved in El Malik v. McDonough
as res judicata bars Mr. El Malik from again litigating this already-resolved dispute.

13493: Issue preclusion: WARF I precludes WARF II's doctrine-of-equivalents infringement claims against the A9 and A10 processors, invoked by Apple.

13494: Kessler doctrine: a prior noninfringement judgment bars the second suit against essentially the same products, invoked by Apple.

13502: Preclusive effect of prior affirmances invalidating claims 1-10, 12, and 14-30 of the '431 patent in IPR appeals; appeal dismissed as to those claims

13857: Whether the Federal Circuit's prior nonprecedential Apple decision (holding the earlier complaint not facially frivolous) precludes dismissal here; held not precluded under issue preclusion.
